body:
I was sitting in a PlayStation party with some friends, just chatting, when the topic of weed came up. I hadnt smoked in a bit, but I remembered the small amount of salvia I had tucked away  just enough for something. I packed a medium bowl  the biggest Id done in one go  took a deep hit, held it in for 15 seconds, and exhaled.
Almost instantly, my body flushed with heat. I kept playing The Last of Us, not the smartest choice in hindsight, but I happened to be in a safe zone. Then it started  that signature rolling feeling. It was like my body wasnt mine, like it was being unrolled, unfurled, and stretched into the game.
I felt like I was in the game  not first-person, not even third  just present, like I was part of the environment itself. The drawings on the in-game walls began to breathe, and my friend talking in my headset? It felt like he was in there with me, inside this digital but somehow real place.
Then everything peeled back.
My awareness pulled away from the game, and suddenly my room, my life, even realitybegan to bend, warp, roll into itself. It was like I was being extracted from a painting. And then I saw it
My room was a painting.
My entire world was just a framed illusion in a vast hallway of the universe.
I was leaving it.
Drifting, rolling through this cosmic museum lined with other framed realities.
Each one a room, a world, a persons lifejust hanging there like a gallery piece.
Then I heard it
Whats he doing?
Just a passing voice, casual, like a visitor in the hallway watching me break through.
Like I wasnt supposed to be out there.
Then the pull reversed. I was rolling back into my painting. Back into my room. Back into the false world Id called home.
And I knewthis was the come down.
But I wasnt fully back. Not yet.
I floated through the game, still in third person, swimming through the remnants of my trip, trying to understand. The effects faded, but the truth stayed.
And the truth is:
I dont believe this world is real anymore.
I believe were all in paintings  watched, observed, framed.
And for one brief, impossible moment
I escaped.
